lessons.title: CTI is a named API, not a vibe
objectives: Use the API name the page printed
paragraphs: The APIs and SDKs page lists a Computer Telephony Integration (CTI) Web Services API next to Configuration, Reporting, Statistics, Web2Campaign, the CRM SDK, and Web Connectors. CTI, on that page, is one of those names.

Wikipedia's ACD article says an advanced distributor may use computer telephony integration as an input to the route. That is the general word. Five9's page is the product name. A screen pop, a click-to-dial button, and a package version were not on the pages this chapter read.
uncertain: Salesforce screen pop, click-to-dial, and package versions were not on the pages this chapter could read.

paragraphs: The desktop page says that whether you deploy Agent Desktop Plus or a pre-built CRM integration, you get the same underlying technology. It also describes the Agent Desktop Toolkit as REST APIs, reference UIs, and other tools to embed agent functionality in a custom CRM or another CRM.
Same technology is not the same screen. Plus is the Five9 screen. A prebuilt integration is the CRM screen. The toolkit is how you embed. Say which of the three you are looking at.

lessons.title: Workforce tools can show up inside the CRM

The WEM quality list names Salesforce, Zendesk, Oracle, and ServiceNow for that quality integration. Three lists, three pages. A floor can have the voice adapter and not the WFO connector. Ask which list you implemented.

lessons.title: A CRM note you can defend
objectives: Name the surface and the list
paragraphs: A defendable note names the surface, the list, and the gap. Surface: Plus, prebuilt, toolkit, or bookmark. List: the API CRM names, the UC names, or the WFO actions. Gap: anything from an admin guide that did not open, marked confirm, with no URL and no guessed field.

The API page says integrations can often be done with minimal coding. Often and minimal are the page's words. They are not a project estimate. The desktop page's single screen is the agent experience it describes, not a count of browser tabs this lab measured.
uncertain: Project size is not on the API page. Minimal coding is their phrase, not an estimate.
